content:
We have carbon NMR peaks: 161.40, 143.85, 130.30, 26.65, 22.80, 21.35, 19.20 ppm.

We need number of CH3 groups (methyl). Methyl carbons appear around 10-30 ppm. Here we have four peaks in that region: 26.65, 22.80, 21.35, 19.20. Likely each corresponds to a CH3 carbon. So number of methyl groups = 4.

Check if any could be other aliphatic carbons (CH2). But typical CH2 ~20-40 as well. However we have four distinct peaks; could be mixture of CH3 and CH2. Need more info. Could use proton NMR to see methyl signals. Let's get proton NMR.
